encounters.cc: Routine health check-up with request for private sexual health consultation

lines: Routine health check-up with request for private sexual health consultation
She is accompanied by her mother but requests to speak with the physician privately.
Once alone, she expresses concerns about her sexual health, stating that she has recently become sexually active with her boyfriend.
She denies any symptoms of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) but is interested in contraception and STI prevention.
She inquires about the most effective method of contraception that also provides protection against STIs.
Her medical history is unremarkable.
She is up to date on vaccinations, including the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine.
She has no known drug allergies
- Mother: hypothyroidism
- Father: hypertension
- No family history of thromboembolic disease or early cardiovascular disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student.
Her physical examination is within normal limits

encounters.cc: Painless genital ulcer present for 2 weeks

lines: Painless genital ulcer present for 2 weeks
This 17-year-old female returns following prior visits for sexual health and contraceptive counseling.
She presents for evaluation of a painless genital ulcer that appeared 2 weeks ago.
Active Problem List:
- Inconsistent condom use (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Vaginal contraceptive sponge use (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
NKDA
- Mother: hypothyroidism
- Father: hypertension
- No family history of thromboembolic disease or early cardiovascular disease
She is sexually active with multiple partners and does not consistently use barrier protection.
Physical examination reveals a 1.5-cm indurated ulcer with clean base and raised borders on the labia majora, along with bilateral, nontender inguinal lymphadenopathy.
A rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test is positive.
When informed of the diagnosis, she becomes visibly upset and states that she does not want anyone to know about her condition.
She refuses partner notification and asks the physician to keep the diagnosis confidential.

encounters.cc: Fatigue, weight loss, and intermittent abdominal pain for the past two months with 10-week amenorrhea

lines: Fatigue, weight loss, and intermittent abdominal pain for the past two months with 10-week amenorrhea
The patient returns to obstetrics and gynecology two months following evaluation for a genital ulcer, having previously received contraceptive counseling in this department.
She appears anxious and hesitant to speak in the presence of her parents.
On further questioning, after ensuring privacy, she reveals that she has been sexually active with her boyfriend and is concerned she might be pregnant.
She has not had a menstrual period for the last 10 weeks.
Active Problem List:
- Inconsistent condom use (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Vaginal contraceptive sponge use (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Primary syphilis (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
She has no known drug allergies
- Mother: hypothyroidism
- Father: hypertension
- No family history of thromboembolic disease or early cardiovascular disease
She denies the use of alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs.
She expresses fear about her parents finding out and requests that this information remains confidential.
She denies any suicidal or homicidal ideation, and there is no evidence of abuse or neglect.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
Physical examination is notable for mild lower abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding.
A urine pregnancy test is positive.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe right lower quadrant pain that began 3 hours ago with history of similar intermittent episodes

lines: Sudden onset of severe right lower quadrant pain that began 3 hours ago with history of similar intermittent episodes
This 19-year-old female with prior early pregnancy and history of contraceptive counseling and genital ulcer evaluation presents to the Emergency Department.
She describes the pain as sharp and constant.
She reports that she has experienced similar, but less severe, episodes over the past two months, which resolved spontaneously.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.
She denies any sexual activity, vaginal discharge, or bleeding.
Active Problem List:
- Inconsistent condom use (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Vaginal contraceptive sponge use (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Primary syphilis (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- Early pregnancy (first trimester) (diagnosed 2021-05-15)
NKDA
- Mother: hypothyroidism
- Father: hypertension
- No family history of thromboembolic disease or early cardiovascular disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student.
Her vital signs are stable
On examination, she appears to be in distress due to pain.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness and a palpable mass in the right adnexal region.
There is no rebound tenderness or guarding.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Pelvic ultrasound shows an enlarged right ovary with peripheral follicles and decreased blood flow.

lines: Acute onset of severe right lower quadrant pain that started 6 hours ago with nausea and vomiting

She denies any vaginal discharge or bleeding, urinary symptoms, or recent illness.

lines: Severe lower abdominal pain radiating to the back that started 6 hours ago with associated nausea
The patient returns with recurrent abdominal pain, having presented similarly in January 2024 and 2023, and describes pain that started 6 hours ago.
The pain is constant, sharp, and radiates to her back.
She reports nausea but no vomiting, fever, or changes in bowel or bladder habits.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain present for 6 hours

lines: Sudden-onset, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain present for 6 hours
The patient returns with recurrent right lower quadrant pain, having presented with similar episodes in 2023, 2024, and 2025.
She presents to the emergency department with a 6-hour history of sudden-onset, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain.
She describes the pain as sharp and constant.
She denies any nausea, vomiting, or fever.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.
Active Problem List:
- Inconsistent condom use (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Vaginal contraceptive sponge use (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Primary syphilis (diagnosed 2021-03-15)
- Early pregnancy (first trimester) (diagnosed 2021-05-15)
- Ovarian Torsion (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
She takes no medications.
NKDA
- Mother: hypothyroidism
- Father: hypertension
- No family history of thromboembolic disease or early cardiovascular disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: High school student.
On physical examination, her vital signs are stable,
She appears to be in distress due to pain.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness and guarding in the right lower quadrant with no rebound tenderness.
A pelvic examination shows a tender, palpable mass in the right adnexal region.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals an enlarged, edematous right ovary with decreased blood flow.
